design: MemoryOperationsService (Codex checkpoint, unchanged semantics) authenticates the binding, matches the full isolation tuple of the requested partition to the verified GCS before any inventory, asks the live operations policy and stop epoch, inventories only committed heads of that partition and rechecks deadline, policy and stop epoch after each effect; monitoring returns bounded counts of the authorised partition only and metric labels are (operation, outcome, reason_code).

Pressure and retention select deterministically (due time, item id), never select LEGAL_HOLD items, and delete only through the existing 0055 lifecycle saga (DELETION_PENDING -> DELETED | DELETION_INCOMPLETE); tombstones are never removed and partial deletions keep the item counted.

MemoryQuotaWriter applies the configured item, payload, embedding-dimension, index-entry and retention limits to a real admission plus store commit: demand is derived from the actual payload bytes and candidate (not caller counters), the candidate must be bound to the plan GCS and owner, inventory, quota check, admission and store commit run inside the trusted partition serialization port, and missing audit/policy/serialization/stop authority never reaches admission. Exact replay and same-item correction at capacity are accepted.

MemoryBackupService captures, through the same guarded envelope, a canonical digest-only manifest of the authorised partition: per head the version, lifecycle status, deletion epoch, content ref and digest, stage digest, item digests and audit refs of every version and the representation kinds/versions/digests/epochs, plus the deletion journal checkpoint read before and after the inventory (refused if it changed), the bounded usage and the trusted recovery point identity; the bytes are signed by the backup custodian port.

MemoryRestoreGate opens restored memory only after: exact-true custodian verification, closed canonical manifest decoding, the recovery point identity, a deletion-authority checkpoint not older than the manifest (otherwise STALE_DELETION_EPOCH before any purge), DeletionRestoreGate.reconcile (tombstone replay before any comparison) and an exact comparison of the restored metadata/ledger with the manifest; items deleted after the backup must carry the replayed authoritative tombstone epoch, every other item must match head, stage, partition, version digests and item/pointer deletion epochs, and an extra restored item is projection drift. serve repeats the comparison before and after the materialising callback inside the 0056 gate; any failure closes the boundary.

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 Part II 2.13 lists the backup manifest members; restore must replay tombstones before reopening retrieval and projection drift or a stale deletion epoch blocks materialisation. A deletion-authority checkpoint older than the manifest is read as a stale deletion epoch (journal rollback) and refused before any purge, the most restrictive reading.

The store snapshots themselves are the OCOR-DEV-0049/0056 recovery-point procedure; this task binds the memory manifest to that recovery point identity and verifies the restored projection against it. No RTO/RPO, EV-031 or recovery conformance is claimed.

Quota exceedance produces a refusal (quota/backpressure), never semantic downgrade (ADD v1.3 Part II 2.13): no representation is dropped to fit a limit and the boundary-value write is accepted with all representations.

Backlog requirement BR-003 is the generic task requirement; following the sealed G5 practice the cases are also bound to FR-118 (lifecycle, legal hold, deletion and restore tests of ADD v1.3 Part II section 3) and NFR-033 (quota behaviour) as component-level evidence only; the G6 binding of NFR-033 remains with OCOR-DEV-0061.

requirement_results.command: The seven configured PoC limits are positive configuration values; quota checks count committed heads once and keep tombstoned/partially deleted items counted; real admission plus store commit on PostgreSQL 16, Qdrant and OpenBao derive demand from the actual payload and candidate, refuse the over-limit item, payload, embedding dimensions and index entries with an audited denial and no ledger entry, version or index entry, accept the exact boundary with every representation (no semantic downgrade), accept exact replay and same-item correction at capacity, and serialize two concurrent writers on a shared PostgreSQL advisory lock (exactly one committed, one ITEM_QUOTA_EXCEEDED); a lock timeout or a missing audit, policy, serialization or stop authority never reaches admission

Quota pressure and retention select deterministically by due time and item id, never select or evict a legal hold (also when placed during the policy check), forget only through the 0055 deletion saga, keep durable tombstones, refuse unknown retention policies and an unavailable audit before any deletion, on the real memory stack and tombstone journal

Monitoring, quota and pressure read only the authorised full isolation partition: unverified bindings and partitions outside the verified GCS never reach policy or inventory, an unauthorised partition cannot change counts, quota decisions, pressure or metric labels (fixed label set), policy/audit/stop/inventory failures and malformed envelopes fail closed with an audited denial and never return zero usage or success

The backup manifest of the authorised partition is canonical, digest-only and signed (OpenBao transit in the live cases) and records memory metadata, content refs, representation versions, lifecycle and deletion epochs, the deletion journal checkpoint and per-version audit refs bound to the recovery point; binding, policy, checkpoint outage or race, signer failure, invalid recovery point, foreign partition and audit failure produce no manifest

On the real 0056 backup drill (PostgreSQL snapshot copy, Qdrant snapshot recovery, OpenBao attestation) restored memory stays closed until the manifest is authenticated, bound to the recovery point and not newer than the deletion authority, every tombstone is replayed through the 0056 gate and the restored projection equals the manifest; a deletion after the backup is never resurrected, a held item stays held, an unauthenticated or foreign manifest purges nothing, a stale deletion epoch is refused before any purge, projection drift (older restored version, extra item, drift during materialisation) and a missing journal keep or close the boundary

residual_risks: The operations policy, hold registry, quota serialization, audit store and backup custodian of the qualifying cases are test adapters on the real PostgreSQL and OpenBao; no production authority service exists yet (open, unassigned).

The final control check and the effects at the independent lifecycle, audit and store authorities are not one transaction; a store commit failure after admission can leave a PENDING version handled by the existing reconciliation (open, tracked toward FGM-17; not claimed closed).
The restore checkpoint port must be the same trusted deletion authority composed into the DeletionRestoreGate; the composition is a deployment obligation, not enforced by type.

Quotas count committed logical heads and native representation slots, not historical journal or object bytes; process-local serialization would not qualify cross-worker use (only the shared PostgreSQL adapter is qualified).
Manifest and audit digests are non-content references that may be correlatable; the membership-inference risk declared in 0055 remains open and unassigned.
